title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a tame ('modérée') topology. The basic data is a 'contrée' C = (𝓕, ≤, ≼). Here 𝓕 is a set of 'figures', F' ≤ F means F' is a subdivision of F, and X ≼ F means X is a sub-figure of F. There is also a disjointness relation between figures. Each figure has a 'cospectre' (apparently the set of figures disjoint from it) and a 'support' (its trace on an underlying set M of points). Axiom C5 on the previous page says: if F' ≤ F, then any figure G is disjoint from F iff it is disjoint from F'.

This page draws the consequences.
(1) C5 holding for all G is equivalent to F and F' having the same cospectre. Once a support map is given, this is also equivalent to F and F' having the same support. So subdivision does not change the 'point-set' content.
(2) Restated as 'F, G disjoint ⟹ F', G disjoint', this yields a Corollary. For every object G, its cospectre in 𝓕 is closed:
  - under ≤, by C5 (both directions);
  - under ≼ (a sub-figure of a figure disjoint from G is disjoint from G, presumably an earlier disjointness axiom).
  It is therefore (a fortiori) a sub-contrée.
(3) The same holds for the cospectre of any subset 𝒢 ⊂ 𝓕, since this is the intersection of the cospectres of its members.
(4) Equivalently, any 'F-support' or '𝓕-stable' subset of Ob 𝓕 is automatically a sub-contrée.
The next page then formally defines a sub-contrée: closed for ≤ and stable under finite sups for ≤ (corresponding to closed parts M' of M), and closed for ≼. The purpose is to build the analogue of closed subspaces, and of restriction to them, inside the axiomatic tame-topology framework.
errors: Gap relative to Definition 1 on p.71: a sub-contrée must also be stable under finite sups for ≤. The corollary does not check that a cospectre is stable under finite sups. This needs an axiom that a sup of figures disjoint from G is disjoint from G; it is presumably available among the disjunction axioms but is not invoked here.
The equivalence 'same cospectre ⟺ same support' presupposes that support is defined from (or determined by) the cospectre. This is a definitional matter, not proved on the page.

ideas.what: Subdivision-invariance of disjointness: subdivisions have the same cospectre/support
ideas.modern_name: invariance of underlying point-set/support under subdivision (cf. polyhedra, semi-algebraic or o-minimal cell decompositions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (Poincaré, Alexander); o-minimal formalism of van den Dries
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5, but this axiomatic 'contrée' formalism is not published

ideas.what: Cospectre of a figure (or set of figures) is automatically a sub-contrée, i.e. a 'closed sub-structure'
ideas.modern_name: closed sub-object / closed sublocale defined by an orthogonality (disjointness) condition; restriction of a definable structure to a definable closed set
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in locale/frame theory and o-minimal geometry

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'contrée' (𝓕, ≤ subdivision, ≼ sub-figure, disjointness) as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; comparable to o-minimal structures or point-free (lattice-theoretic) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimality, 1980s-1998), Shiota; Grothendieck only programmatically
ideas.where_published: Only the programme in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6; the 1986 notes remain unpublished

missed.claim: This page is a building block of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic framework for tame topology ('contrées' built from figures, subdivision ≤ and sub-figure ≼). It is a point-free, order-theoretic alternative to o-minimal structures that was never developed. Together with the 'modérée' condition on p.69 (any two subdivisions are comparable, a Hauptvermutung-type axiom), it suggests a programme comparing this axiomatics with o-minimal triangulation theorems. That comparison does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: toute partie de 𝓕 qui est un 𝓕-support ... est automatiquement une sous-contrée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would give a lattice- or locale-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology. It could be compared with o-minimal definable sets and with the locale/frame approach. The page itself contains only a routine lemma, however.

deep.surprise_reason: The page proves a routine corollary inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. The framework as a whole is a little-known thread, but this page adds no notable result.
transcription_corrections: 'c'est donc un fermé [?] quelle [?] une sous-contrée' more plausibly reads 'c'est donc a fortiori une sous-contrée' (uncertain).
'Le cospectre [-de-] {+dans 𝓕+}' — the insertion above the line seems to be 'dans 𝓕', correct.
'de (Ob 𝓕)' may read 'cf (Ob 𝓕)' or 'de Ob 𝓕' — uncertain.
The marginal parenthesis reads roughly '(ou "𝓕-stable", si on entend : un terme de ≤,)' — uncertain.
